<?php

$baseUrl = 'https://api.spryng.nl/v2/webhooks/authentication-methods';
$ch = curl_init();
curl_setopt($ch, CURLOPT_URL, $baseUrl);

$headers = [
     'AccountReference' => 'your-AccountReference-header-here',
     'X-Api-Key' => 'YOUR_KEY_HERE'
    ];

curl_setopt($ch, CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER, $headers);


    $body = json_encode([
  "oauth" => [
    "clientIdValue" => "clientIdValue",
    "clientIdPropertyName" => "clientIdPropertyName",
    "clientSecretValue" => "clientSecretValue",
    "clientSecretPropertyName" => "clientSecretPropertyName",
    "tokenUrl" => "tokenUrl",
    "accessTokenPropertyName" => "accessTokenPropertyName"
  ],
  "apiKey" => [
    "key" => "key",
    "value" => "value",
    "asQueryParam" => false
  ],
  "basic" => [
    "username" => "username",
    "password" => "password",
    "token" => "token"
  ]
]);
        
curl_setopt($ch, CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER, true);

$response = curl_exec($ch);
$info = curl_getinfo($ch);

curl_close($ch);

if ($info['http_code'] >= 400) {
    echo 'Error! HTTP code: ' . $info['http_code'] . ', Response: ' . $response;
} else {
    echo 'Success! Response: ' . $response;
}

sections.title: API overview
sections.content:
This endpoint can be used to increase the authentication required for webhooks on an account. This increases security for webhooks used, meaning a consumer can verify they’re receiving a webhook from an expected source and the webhook producer can verify the customer.

There are 3 possible authentication methods available:
  • Basic Authentication/ Username & Password
  • OAuth Verification Token/ Bearer Token
  • Custom Headers/ API Key

A maximum of one authentication method can be set per account.If the type of the authentication method is updated, this is automatically reflected on all existing subscriptions of that account.If more than one authentication method is specified, the request will fail with a 400 status code.

sections.title: Headers
sections.content:
These parameters are mandatory to be provided in the header of your request. If not provided, or incorrect, your request will fail.

HeaderTypeDescription
X-Api-KeyStringAPI Key value for authorization
AccountReferenceStringYour Esendex account reference - e.g. SPNL0000000

Example request header:
PUT https://api.spryng.nl/v2/webhooks/authentication-methods
-H 'Api-Key: YOUR_API_KEY'
-H 'AccountReference: SPNL0000000'

sections.title: OAuth Verification Token
sections.content:
Token (bearer) authentication is a standard method to authenticate webhooks. This is an OAuth verification protocol that allows users to verify their identity on a web application, receive an access token and verify each request to the web app with the access token. The authenticated request uses the authorization header to send the token using the format below:
authorization: Bearer {token}

Webhook consumers can use this strategy to authenticate webhook requests arriving at the webhook URL.
OAuth 2.0 requires an authentication token, which is issued by an authorization server, in order to connect to customer webhook endpoint. The authentication token is checked by the receiving endpoint when accepting the HTTP request.
To configure OAuth 2.0, customers need to provide the following information:
  • OAuth2 Client ID and OAuth2 Client Secret that the platform will use to request the authentication token from your authorization server
  • OAuth2 Token URL i.e. the URL of the authorization server from which the platform will request the token

Once this has been configured, you then need to define the authentication method during webhook subscription creation/editing. This can be done specifying the authentication method Id.
Once set up, the platform will request a token when we are attempting to send data to the webhook target. We also request a token when a webhook is initially created, or later modified/updated.

OAuth required headers

PropertyTypeDescription
clientIdValueStringClient ID that the platform will use to request the authentication token from customer authorization server
clientSecretIdPropertyValueStringClient Secret that the platform will use to request the authentication token from customer authorization server
clientSecurityValueStringThe secret value specified for authentication
clientSecretPropertyNameStringThe name of the secret value
tokenUrlStringContains the URL the authorization server from which the platform will request the token
accessTokenPropertyNameStringThe name given to the access token

Example 
PUT v2/webhooks/authentication-method

[
  {
    "client_id": "message-failed",
    "client_secret": "string",
    "token_url": "string"
  }
]

sections.title: API Key auth
sections.content:
Custom headers/ API Key authentication required headers

PropertyTypeDescription
keyStringAPI key
valueStringAPI key value
asQueryParamBooleanDefault = “false”. Needs to be set to “True” to use this authentication method.

Example 
PUT v2/webhooks/authentication-method

{
  "apiKey":{
    "key": "string",
    "value": "string",
    "asQueryParam": "True"
  }
}

sections.title: Basic auth
sections.content:
Basic authentication/ username & password required headers

PropertyTypeDescription
usernameStringUsername if using basic authentication
passwordStringPassword if using basic authentication
basicTokenStringBasic token if using basic token authentication

Example
PUT v2/webhooks/authentication-method

{
  "basic":{
    "username": "string",
    "password": "string",
    "token": "string"
  }
}

sections.title: Responses
sections.content:
The standard responses for this API are listed below. For a full list of possible REST API status codes, please refer to this guide.

Success
201 Created
Success response
Errors
400 Bad Request
The server could not understand the request due to incorrect syntax or an incorrect/missing required property. You should not repeat the request without modifications.
{
    "errors": [
        {
            "errorCode": "error_code",
            "errorMessage": "error_message"
        }
    ]
}

401 Unauthorized
Indicates that the request has failed due to missing or incorrect authentication information. You can repeat the request with a suitable authorization header field.
{
    "errors": [
        {
            "errorCode": "unauthenticatedError",
            "errorMessage": "Request for authenticated route '/v2/webhooks/authentication-methods' was unauthenticated"
        }
    ]
}
